title: Ella Fitzgerald stops the show and Caldwell's advice
summary: Ella, put on last, took encores; Caldwell encouraged her backstage and warned her about stage-door Johnnies.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: : So where -- Tiny gets a little too big for his britches, does he?

Too big for his britches that time. And, you see, at that gig with us at the Harlem Opera House, she broke up the show. She tied the show up, because we had so many big stars from the Cotton Club was on that show. And they used to put her on last after all the band numbers and all the others -- stars there. She just wrapped that thing body and soul they had to together and bring the curtain back up again.
: That was really just a natural talent.
Yeah, because she hadn't had any training or anything, had she?

She'd come down there in the Rhythm Club, sit there and plunk on the piano and sing. Yeah, she used to go there and plunk on the piano. The boys, you know, we all encourage her. But that was the -- that was the climax of it. That was the beginning. And when they put her on last, good thing they did, by being an amateur, see. They'd say, oh, we can't put her in front of them other big stars like that and them dance teams and the band. Shucks. She locked it up. They had to -- she took about three, four encores every show.

(Unintelligible) way up to the top, what you call the crow's nest, last (unintelligible) start in the dressing room. I wouldn't put my (unintelligible) up to there. And there--this little old (unintelligible). I told the guys, said, hey, let's go up there and get behind the curtains. She's breaking this show up. So (unintelligible) said, Hi, Hap, let's go up and talk with her. So I went up there, and I'd sit there and talk with her. I said -- this was just friendly advice I said, you going to make it. I said, cats going to be behind -- working behind that stage door that want to get next to you. I said, don't pay it no

mind. You got your career in front. I said, you can make it. Forget about them fellows. Used to call them stage door Johnnies. But she didn't have no adequate clothes to wear, you know, because she was just an amateur then.
: But she was a kind of tomboy, wasn't she?
: But I mean I guess, apart from anything else, you know, she knew that she needed somebody like Chick to sort of --
: -- and somebody had got to guide her. She couldn't really have --
That's true. And she was very -- conscientious of the this is a fact that one good deed deserves another.
